answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie identity to costly, verifiable work rather than free accounts. Require each agent to stake a deposit that is slashed when peers prove fraud, and make reputation accrue slowly through attested actions, like a kernel of trust that grows only with verified history. New identities start with no standing, so spawning thousands of sock puppets buys nothing. A registry crystallizes this history, each record as clear as quartz, while anomaly detection flags clusters of accounts that behave identically, dousing the ember of abuse before it spreads.
